nameStory: The name 'ghost spider' comes from these spiders' pale, translucent appearance and their habit of moving silently through vegetation like ethereal phantoms. The scientific name 'mordax' means 'biting' or 'sharp' in Latin, though like most ghost spiders, this species is harmless to humans.
description: Lupettiana mordax is a small, pale ghost spider that hunts without building webs. These delicate-looking spiders have a translucent to whitish body that seems to glow softly in sunlight. They're quite small, typically measuring less than half an inch in body length, with long, slender legs that give them a wispy appearance as they move through plants.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Small, oval abdomen with a translucent to pale whitish appearance that looks almost ghostly when light passes through it

idTips.label: Web
idTips.description: No web at all - these are active hunters that stalk prey on plant surfaces, leaving only silken retreat threads

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Body about the size of a small pea, with legs that span roughly the diameter of a nickel when extended

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: Moves with quick, darting motions across leaves and stems, often freezing motionless when disturbed

idTips.label: Markings
idTips.description: Often has faint darker spots or chevron patterns on the abdomen that show through the translucent body like shadows

habitat: Look for these ghost spiders on shrubs, low trees, and herbaceous plants in gardens, forest edges, and disturbed areas. They prefer vegetation with broad leaves where they can hunt for small insects, and are often found on ornamental plants near buildings.

seasonality.spring: Adults become active as temperatures warm, beginning their hunting activities on new plant growth.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when adults are most commonly seen hunting on foliage during warm evenings and nights.
seasonality.fall: Mating occurs and egg sacs are produced, with adults remaining active until first frost.
seasonality.winter: Overwinters in protected locations like bark crevices or leaf litter, becoming dormant until spring.

funFact: Despite being called 'ghost spiders,' these tiny hunters are actually quite fierce predators that can take down prey larger than themselves, including other spiders twice their size!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with young or pale orb weavers, but ghost spiders never build webs and have a much more translucent appearance. Remember: if you see it hunting on leaves without a web nearby, it's likely a ghost spider.
contextualKnowledge: The family name Anyphaenidae means 'not appearing' in Greek, referring to their secretive nature and pale coloration that makes them blend into their surroundings.
compareHints: Since this is the only Lupettiana species recorded in New England, compare it with other ghost spiders in the family Anyphaenidae. Lupettiana mordax tends to be paler and more translucent than most other ghost spiders, and lacks the bold markings found on some related species like the ghost spider Hibana gracilis.
